title: A finite type sheaf lives on a finitely presented closed subscheme with prescribed fibre support
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$. Write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field] and let $\mathcal F_s$ be the pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $X_s$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. There exist a closed immersion $j:Z\to X$ of finite presentation [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal H$ such that $j_*\mathcal H\cong\mathcal F$ and the underlying closed subset $|Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)|$ of $|X_s|$ equals $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)=\{u\in X_s:(\mathcal F_s)_u\ne0\}$, with $(\mathcal F_s)_u$ the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Here $j_*\mathcal H(V)=\mathcal H(j^{-1}V)$ for open subsets $V\subseteq X$.

proof.text: Write X=Spec(B), S=Spec(A), and let A→B be the ring map induced by f. Put M=Γ(X,F); since F is quasi-coherent on the affine scheme X, the counit ~M→F of the tilde/global-sections adjunction is an isomorphism, so F≅~M. Since f is finite type, the affine-pairs characterization gives that A→B is a finite-type ring map. Since F is quasi-coherent of finite type on the affine X, M is a finite B-module. Put I=Ann_B(M). The affine support computation identifies Supp(F) with V(I) in Spec(B).

Let p⊂A be the prime corresponding to s and put R=B⊗_Aκ(p). By the affine fibre-product formula, X_s≅Spec(R) with the projection X_s→X equal to Spec of b↦b⊗1. By the tilde-pullback base-change isomorphism (and (h∘g)^*≅g^*h^* for composition with this isomorphism), F_s≅~(R⊗_BM)=~(M⊗_Aκ(p)). The support-pullback theorem gives Supp(F_s) as the inverse image of Supp(F)=V(I) under Spec(R)→Spec(B); a prime Q of R contains the image of I iff its contraction contains I, so this inverse image is V(IR), where IR is the ideal generated by the image of I. (The tensor module is finite over R because a finite generating family of M remains a finite generating family after tensoring.)

The ring R is a finite-type algebra over the field κ(p), so it is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-a-field Noetherian lemma. Therefore the ideal IR is generated by finitely many elements. Choose f_1,…,f_m∈I whose images generate IR, and let J=(f_1,…,f_m)⊂B. Then JR=IR.

Let Z=Spec(B/J) and let j:Z→X be Spec of the quotient map B→B/J. By the affine pushforward formula j_*O_Z≅~(B/J), so O_X=~B→j_*O_Z is surjective, and j is a homeomorphism onto V(J); hence j is a closed immersion. Because J is generated by finitely many elements, B/J≅B[]/(f_1,…,f_m) is a finite presentation of B over itself with no variables, so j is locally of finite presentation; it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated as a morphism of affine schemes, hence of finite presentation. Since J⊂I, M is naturally a B/J-module; let H=~M on Z. H is quasi-coherent, and of finite type since its global sections M are finitely generated over B/J (the finite B-module generators of M). The affine pushforward formula gives j_*H≅~(M_B)=~M≅F by Step 1.

By the affine fibre-product formula, Z×_S Spec κ(p)≅Spec((B/J)⊗_Aκ(p))=Spec(R/JR) (right exactness of the tensor product), and its map to X_s=Spec(R) is Spec of R→R/JR, whose image is the closed subset V(JR)=V(IR) of Spec(R) (Step 3). By the support computation in Step 2 this is exactly Supp(F_s), proving the required equality of underlying closed subsets.

tool_uses.why: Affine finite-type ring-map characterization needed to pass from the morphism hypothesis to A→B finite type; this trace-formula unit has no such algebra lemma.
Affine quasi-coherent finite-type modules correspond to finite modules and provide the finite-type sheaf H; this is a generic affine module tool.
Affine support equals the annihilator zero locus for F; this generic support theorem is not supplied by the trace-formula unit.
The fibre support is the inverse image of Supp(F) under pullback; the unit has no fibre-support comparison theorem.
A finite-type algebra over a field is Noetherian, so the fibre extension ideal has finitely many generators; this algebra theorem is outside the unit route.
Step 2 identifies the fibre module F_s with the tilde of M⊗_Aκ(p); this affine pullback formula is a generic module tool not supplied by the trace-formula unit (added by the maintainer reader).
